title: Top-down GTA-ish game I'm making in Godot. Help me with the direction
author: LogMysterious3056
selftext:
The tiles, buildings, cars, people, the font and the sounds are all generated in GDScript at startup. There isn't a single png in the whole thing.

The clip has two halves. The first one is the loud version, basically GTA2. The second is where I've been taking it lately, which is more about stealth and not getting spotted.

I can't decide which one the game should be, so two questions: does it actually look decent, and which half would you want to play?

comments.author: Feeling_Coyote_513
comments.body: How does it generate the tiles, buildings, people, etc.? Can you explain that part

replies.author: LogMysterious3056
replies.body:
How it works, step by step:  
1. Basic shapes → tiny textures. Functions like rect(), circle(), ellipse() build a small Image pixel-by-pixel in memory (looping over x/y, computing a color per pixel with math like "distance from center"), then convert it to a Texture2D Godot can draw. A blue rectangle isn't a file - it's 40 lines of code that fill pixels blue

2. 3D-looking models from flat slices (models.gd). A car or person is built as a stack of horizontal "slices" -rounded boxes and ellipses drawn with a signed-distance-field formula (rrect, ellipse), which gives smooth anti-aliased edges plus fake shading (a highlight on one side, a dark rim on the other) so a flat pixel blob reads as a rounded 3D volume

3. Buildings, every single frame (skyline.gd). Walls and roofs aren't pre-drawn either - they're recomputed and redrawn every frame based on the camera position, because the projection math (cam + (p - cam) \* scale) depends on where the camera is. Nothing can be "baked" into a static image and just moved around.

Caching, so it's not slow. Since generating pixels one-by-one is expensive, results get cached by a key (e.g. "rect\_64\_32\_#ff0000\_...") in a Dictionary - the shape is built once and reused after that, so the game doesn't regenerate a red rectangle every time it needs one.
